findings.issue: voidedBets re-implements liveLevels' voiding walk (folded set from other streets, put map, preflop big-blind floor, strict-top test). Nothing ties the two together, so a future change to the voiding rule in liveLevels would silently leave advice classifying against a different rule than the engine's currentBet/betCount.
findings.evidence: Lines 361-387 repeat liveLevels lines 330-350 nearly verbatim. I fuzzed 20,000 random 2-10 seat hands with random forced folds (184,290 states, 9,830 with a void) and compared liveLevels (copied) with a plain full-bet level walk that skips the indices voidedBets returns. There were 0 mismatches, so the two agree today. The playtest output (10,000 hands, seed 42) is byte-identical to base_commit's.
findings.fix: Optional: drop the voiding branch from liveLevels and have it skip `voidedBets(state)` indices in its level walk (the fuzz shows this is equivalent), so one function owns the rule. If you'd rather leave liveLevels untouched, add a short comment on each function pointing to the other, saying they must stay in step.

summary: Every SPEC item is implemented and tested, and none of the tests could pass against a broken implementation. Reverting the situationOf filter fails SPEC-01, and over-voiding fails SPEC-02 (hand P). voidedBets agrees with liveLevels' voiding rule: 0 mismatches over 184k fuzzed states. The ring tidy-up and the sole hoist are equivalent, and the 10k-hand playtest is byte-identical to base with 0 invariant violations. The new tests, the force-fold suites, lint and typecheck all pass. Only a MINOR (the voiding rule is duplicated) and a NIT. No BLOCKER or MAJOR.
